entries.title: The ayanāṃśa from the paramparā's three determinations: the text's libration fitted on its phase and its greatest value
entries.derives: Āryabhaṭa states the ayanāṃśa was zero in Kali 3600 (499 CE); Nīlakaṇṭha works an eclipse with 14°26′ at Kali day 1,643,524 (1398); Parameśvara 'determined by testing' 15° complete in Kali 4536 (1435). The text's libration (SS 3.9-3.10) has two parameters, its phase and its greatest value (27° + δ); fitted to the three records by least squares they come out phase 0.001°, δ = +1.8613° — Āryabhaṭa's zero stands and the swing widens, so the rate grows from 54″ to 57.72″ a year, the rate his zero and Nīlakaṇṭha's figure imply between them. Residuals 0.0, −0.5, +0.5′. A single record cannot tell a phase from an amplitude change; the phase-only reading of the morning met the two Kerala figures but broke Āryabhaṭa's zero by 57.6′ and was superseded the same day (owner: adopt every improvement the records support). The default choice applies both parameters; the Kerala choice runs a line through the same three records (0.9620′ a year, its zero at Kali 3600.0).

entries.title: The resolution the vargas demand: exact varga indices and margins, the 108-lattice, the daśā's sensitivity
entries.derives: The sixteen vargas of BPHS ch.6 (and D-144, D-150 as standard higher divisions) computed exactly in micro-arcseconds: for any longitude the varga sign, the part, and the distance to the nearest edge; a placement 'decided' only when that distance exceeds the choice's measured uncertainty. The time one part is worth for given rates (lagna seconds, Moon minutes, Sun hours). The lattice 27 × 4 = 108 = 12 × 9 with the theorem that one pāda is one navāṃśa, the 27 → 9 Vimśottarī lord projection, and the daśā days per minute of arc of the Moon (BPHS 46.16).

entries.title: Time from one turn of the star-wheel: civil day, spandas, Kali day, vāra
entries.derives: From SS 1.11–1.12 one turn of the star-wheel (nākṣatra ahorātra) is 60 nāḍī = 21,600 prāṇa = 360°: time is the angle turned, and on the 328,050,000,000-spanda lattice 1″ = 253,125, 1 prāṇa = 1′. By SS 1.34 a body's own risings are star-risings less its revolutions, so three integers (risings, Sun, Moon; SS 1.29–1.34) yield civil days, lunar/solar months, adhimāsa, tithis, tithikṣaya (1.35–1.39, 14.14); Āryabhaṭa's canon (Gītikā 3) too. Adds civil date ↔ Kali-ahargaṇa and vāra, and the kapāla's turn-nāḍī → civil-spanda identity (1.12, 13.23), feeding mean motions by the civil day (14.19).

entries.title: The dhruva frame: the fixed point, obliquity SS 2.28, ecliptic ↔ equatorial
entries.derives: From SS 12.72-12.73, 12.43-44, 13.4 and 8.1-8.15, dhruva.js finds the dhruva POINT (the axis of the turn, not the star near it) from observation: latitude = mean of a circumpolar star's two meridian altitudes; true north = midpoint of its two greatest elongations; ε and latitude = half-difference and half-sum of the two solstitial noon zenith distances, all exact rationals. SS 2.28's sine 1397 on R 3438 is the default ε. It then converts polar (dhruvaka, vikṣepa) ↔ equatorial ↔ ecliptic for the ch.8 star catalogue, 8.15 conjunctions and the time frame of kala-dvara.js.

SS 12.43-12.44: at the equator both dhruvas lie on the horizon
SS 12.72: the dhruva's elevation is the measure of where one stands (latitude)

entries.title: The Kaṭapayādi codec, corrected, tested on the texts' own numbers
entries.derives: A letter-to-digit cipher from the rule verse nañāvacaśca śūnyāni…, commonly attributed to the Sadratnamālā: क…झ and ट…ध = 1–9 with ञ, न = 0; प…म = 1–5; य…ह = 1–8, ळ = 9; a lone vowel = 0; a conjunct counts only its last consonant (kṣa = 6), a vowel-less consonant nothing; aṅkānāṃ vāmato gatiḥ makes the first syllable the units digit. BigInt decoding from Devanāgarī or IAST, checked on Nīlakaṇṭha's Jyotirmīmāṃsā ahargaṇas and Śakābda constants, Mādhava's Rsines, two candravākyas, the melakarta rule and the π verse; it feeds the engine's reading of ahargaṇas and constants from the texts (§3).

entries.title: Mādhava's sine (R = 3437′44″48‴) as the exact default sine
entries.derives: Mādhava's R-sine (Kerala), as Nīlakaṇṭha's school records it in five Kaṭapayādi words, is evaluated as an exact rational polynomial on radius 3437′44″48‴ with q = 5400′: Rsin x = x − (x/q)³[c₁ − (x/q)²[c₂ − (x/q)²[c₃ − (x/q)²[c₄ − (x/q)²c₅]]]]. Since 2026-10-07 it replaces the Sūrya-Siddhānta's 24-entry table (SS 2.17-2.22, 2.31-2.33) as the default sine in the manda equation (2.29-2.45) and the true motion (2.47-2.49), so the Sun, Moon and every pañcāṅga limb stay exact fractions on the spanda lattice; sphuta.js and the SS modules carry the same coefficients to R = 3438.

SS 2.34: epicycles Sun 14°/13°40′, Moon 32°/31°40′

entries.method: Horner evaluation in BigInt, with c₁…c₅ in thirds and x/q as X/B, gives Rsin as an exact fraction; the arc is the first point of a lattice 10,000 times finer than the arc-spanda whose sine reaches the value, by integer bisection (not a Mādhava rule). Tests compare the table and Mādhava tiers (withSine) on the same dates, and both against Math.sin, which appears only to measure.

DOP853 is the n-body engine; IAS15 the Gauss–Radau under test; radau.js the owner's 15th-order Gauss–Radau, nodes the roots of P₇+P₈, force a parameter. §13 runs the complete law 74.4 years and feeds the yuga revolutions of apogee and node (§13.5), the Moon's terms (§13.6) and the calendar (§13.7).

entries.title: The 2PN term and its sign, derived from the harmonic Schwarzschild metric
entries.derives: The 2PN term of the engine's force law (dop853-nbody.js, block 3) is computed, not chosen. The only input is the Schwarzschild metric in harmonic coordinates, the gauge of the EIH 1PN block: g_tt = −(r−m)/(r+m), g_ij = (1+m/r)²δ_ij + ((r+m)/(r−m))(m²/r²)n_i n_j. The geodesic equation, with Christoffels taken numerically from that metric, gives the exact coordinate acceleration; its expansion in m/r gives A₂ = 9(m/r)² − 2(m/r)ṙ², B₂ = 2(m/r)ṙ, whose static part is −9m³/r⁴, an attraction. It replaces the old ±3(GM)²/(c⁴r⁴), which is not an acceleration, and feeds the force law and the regenerated corpus (§15.1).
entries.method: Christoffels by central differences (h = 1e-6·|x|) of the harmonic Schwarzschild metric; geodesic equation d²xⁱ/dt² = −Γⁱ_αβuᵅuᵝ + Γᵗ_αβuᵅuᵝvⁱ with u = (1, v); compared with the PN series at orders 0, 1, 2 for m/r = 0.02 down to 0.001 with radial and tangential velocity; a unit-scaling test with λ = AU in km; block 3 of dop853-nbody.js evaluated via evalRhs at m/r = 0.01 and 0.005.

entries.title: The Moon's physical libration by Euler's equations
entries.derives: From the Moon's inertia ratios β=(C−A)/B=6.315e-4, γ=(B−A)/C=2.278e-4, α=4.037e-4, the polar moment C=0.392·M·R² (M=7.342e22 kg, R=1737.4 km), a mean spin of 2π/27.321661 rad/day, and Earth and Sun positions with their GM, the module integrates Euler's rigid-body equations with quaternion kinematics under the gravitational torques of Earth and Sun on the triaxial Moon, giving the physical librations τ (longitude), ρ (latitude), σ (node) in arcseconds and the PA→ME rotation matrix. No text verse is its starting point; no page loads it yet (END-TO-END-REVIEW §4.2).
entries.method: RK4 at 0.05-day steps advances ω by Euler's equations (torques from Earth and Sun on the A,B,C tensor, positions turned into the body frame by the quaternion) and q by q̇=½q⊗ω, renormalising q each step; τ, ρ, σ are read from q against the mean spin angle; R_PA2ME=R_z(−τ)·R_x(−ρ)·R_z(−σ). The test drives it with circular Earth and Sun orbits for 30 days and checks R·Rᵀ=I.

entries.title: Variational state-transition matrix solver for N-body fitting
entries.derives: Along an N-body trajectory the solver integrates, by RK4, the 6N×6N state-transition matrix Φ(t,t0) = ∂Y(t)/∂Y(t0) together with the state, using the exact analytical Jacobian of Newtonian point-mass gravity (the pairwise tidal tensor ∂a_i/∂r_j, with zero-mass tracer bodies guarded). Φ is the sensitivity of later positions and velocities to the starting state, the quantity a fit needs to correct initial conditions from residuals. It starts from no verse or number of a text, and feeds nothing yet: the end-to-end review lists it among the research modules that are tested but loaded by no page.
entries.method: Pure JavaScript, no dependencies. computeGravityJacobian builds the 3N×3N ∂a/∂r from pairwise tidal tensors, each from its own gm so a zero-mass tracer gives no NaN. evalVariationalRhs returns dP/dt=V, dV/dt=A, dΦ/dt=J·Φ. propagateSTM steps Y and Φ by fixed-step RK4 (dt = 0.1 day) from Φ(0)=I to each requested day, returning pos, vel, Φ and its Frobenius norm per sample.

figures.claim: The gravity Jacobian for two bodies comes back with 36 entries, i.e. the 6 × 6 matrix ∂a/∂r for 3N = 6 coordinates.

At the last sample (day 10) the Frobenius norm of the state-transition matrix Φ exceeds 1.0: Φ has grown from the identity.

entries.title: Metric time: TCB−TT and TDB−TT by integrating Earth's proper-time rate
entries.derives: From Earth's heliocentric position and velocity along its trajectory and the GM of the attracting bodies, the module forms the metric clock-rate d(TCB)/dt − 1 = −U/c² − v²/(2c²), integrates it by the trapezoidal rule from Δτ(t₀) ≡ 0 to give TCB−TT in seconds, and subtracts L_B·t to give TDB−TT. It starts from the IAU constants written in the module (c = 299792458 m/s, AU = 149597870.700 km, L_B = 1.550519768e-8), not from any siddhānta verse. It feeds no page: the end-to-end review lists it among the tested research modules awaiting the गणित-शाला page.

entries.title: Candravākya: the Moon's 248 vākyas regenerated from a canon's integers
entries.derives: From a canon's integers — Moon and apogee revolutions per yuga and the yuga's civil days (Āryabhaṭīya Gītikā 3; SS 1.33, 1.37; JM pp.11, 35) — and its manda equation (SS 2.29-2.45) on a sine (SS table 2.17-2.22 or Mādhava's polynomial), the true Moon's advance after n days from the apogee is computed exactly; V(1)…V(248) are the candravākyas, rounded to the second (Mādhava) or minute (Vararuci), written as Kaṭapayādi words. Closure of 248/3031/12,372 days is measured by the canon; vakyaMoon rebuilds the Moon on a Kali day from khaṇḍa, cycle dhruvas and vākya, against the direct sphuṭa.
